message.content:
Below is a **complete, ready‑to‑run example** that shows how to launch a Google Cloud Compute Engine instance that:

* runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**  
* has an **RTX A6000** GPU attached  
* uses a standard machine type (e.g., `n1-standard-8`) – you can adjust the CPU/memory to your needs  
* is created in a specific zone (replace `us-central1-a` with your preferred zone)  

You can use either the **gcloud CLI** (recommended for quick testing) or the **REST API** if you prefer programmatic control. Both approaches are shown below.

---

## 1. Using the `gcloud` CLI

```bash
# 1️⃣  Set your project and zone
PROJECT_ID="your-project-id"
ZONE="us-central1-a"

# 2️⃣  Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE} \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPUs, 30 GB RAM
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --boot-disk-device-name=rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh \   # optional: custom startup script
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --reservation-affinity=any \
  --tags=http-server,https-server
```

### What each flag does

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU & memory allocation |
| `--image-family` / `--image-project` | Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image |
| `--boot-disk-size` | Size of the boot disk |
| `--boot-disk-type` | SSD for faster I/O |
| `--accelerator` | Attach one RTX A6000 GPU |
| `--tags` | Allow HTTP/HTTPS traffic (optional) |
| `--metadata-from-file startup-script` | Run a shell script at first boot (optional) |

> **Tip:** If you need more GPUs, just change `count=2` (or more) – note that the zone must support the requested GPU count.

---

## 2. Using the REST API (JSON)

If you prefer to call the Compute Engine API directly (e.g., from a script or a CI/CD pipeline), use the following JSON payload. Replace placeholders (`YOUR_PROJECT_ID`, `YOUR_ZONE`, etc.) with your actual values.

```json
{
  "name": "rtx-a6000-ubuntu",
  "machineType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/YOUR_ZONE/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "scheduling": {
    "preemptible": false,
    "onHostMaintenance": "MIGRATE",
    "automaticRestart": true
  },
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### Making the API call

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/YOUR_PROJECT_ID/zones/YOUR_ZONE/instances"
```

> **Prerequisites**  
> * Enable the Compute Engine API (`gcloud services enable compute.googleapis.com`).  
> * Ensure your service account has the `roles/compute.instanceAdmin.v1` role.  
> * Make sure the zone you choose supports the RTX A6000 GPU (check [GPU availability](https://cloud.google.com/compute/docs/gpus#availability)).  

---

## 3. Quick sanity check

After creation, verify the instance:

```bash
gcloud compute instances describe rtx-a6000-ubuntu \
  --project=${PROJECT_ID} \
  --zone=${ZONE}
```

Look for the `accelerators` section to confirm the GPU is attached, and the `status` field should read `RUNNING`.

---

### Summary

* **CLI**: `gcloud compute instances create ... --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1`
* **REST**: POST to `/instances` with `guestAccelerators` array containing the RTX A6000 type.

Both methods will give you a fully‑functional Ubuntu 20.04 VM with an RTX A6000 GPU ready for CUDA workloads. Happy computing!
